title: Arrangement for DroneGo
award_status: MCM outstanding paper in the supplied 2019 special-award corpus

source_quality.notes: All 33 physical PDF pages were read in order and visually reviewed through seven byte-bounded page contact sheets and one focused crop. Text extraction preserves most prose, equations, tables, and code but splits mathematical tokens and code lines. Focused review retains the lambda_max glyph ambiguity, Figure 5/Figure 2 mismatch, wrong Table 3 caption, coordinate conflict, body-code weight reversal, ideal-realized-conclusion fleet conflicts, hard-coded 339, and in-place raster mutation rather than silently repairing them. Running team/page headers are excluded from author-language evidence.

context_sources: official 2019 MCM Problem B statement and the supplied DroneGo specifications
summary sheet, complete 30-page printed report body, HELP letter, references, and four appendix code blocks
drone, cargo bay, medicine, container, hospital, road, populated-place, map, and 3DBP inputs invoked by the paper, with missing provenance retained as a gap

task_reconstruction.summary: Design a transportable DroneGo disaster-response plan for Puerto Rico that chooses three container contents and locations, delivers medicine to five hospitals quickly, surveys roads and populated places, schedules repeated flights, and communicates a conditional recommendation to HELP.
inputs: drone types A-H with dimensions, shipping volumes, speed, endurance, payload, camera, and matching cargo-bay specifications
three medicine packages, daily five-hospital demand, container geometry, charging and operating-time premises
hospital coordinates, Puerto Rico coastline, roads, highways, populated places, range circles, and rough-area masks
AHP pairwise judgments, a 120-day floor, common 0.8 loaded-distance factor, packing API, and timetable conventions
outputs: criterion weights and normalized medicine, time, and reconnaissance scores
ideal and realistically packable B-D-H fleets with container-specific medicine inventories and utilization
rough Areas A-C and exact latitude-longitude sites based on delivery, transfer, road, and populated-place evidence
a five-day medicine timetable, reconnaissance allocation, sensitivity results, conclusion, and HELP-facing letter

section_map.summary: title: name the designed system; handoff to summary
abstract: compress the full decision pipeline; handoff to body and HELP letter
introduction: move from context to measurable success; handoff to assumptions
assumptions: state and motivate each simplifying premise; handoff to notation
notation: define symbols with units; handoff to specific formulation
problem-analysis: justify the first discrete decision; handoff to AHP criteria
model-establishment: define, weight, and normalize evaluation factors; handoff to greedy packing
model-improvement: turn ideal scoring into packable container plans; handoff to exact siting and schedules
algorithm: expose executable state transitions; handoff to warning pass
results: trace numerical outputs to decisions; handoff to sensitivity and memo
data-preprocessing: convert maps and service circles into comparable candidate scores; handoff to flight timetable
sensitivity-analysis: perturb inputs and compare decisions; handoff to strengths and weaknesses
strengths: name positive reusable properties; handoff to limitations
limitations: state source-acknowledged boundaries; handoff to conclusion
conclusion: reassemble the answer; handoff to HELP letter
memo: translate the report for HELP leadership; handoff to references
references: separate technical and implementation provenance; handoff to appendix code
appendix: retain implementation evidence; handoff to reproducibility work

assumptions.summary: Loaded maximum distance depends only on drone type and load, with the same proportional reduction applied across drone types.
Drones can be recharged and reused, and every drone type has the same charging time.
Charging is available only at the cargo containers.
Medicine packages may be rotated freely during three-dimensional packing.
Drones, bays, and medicines occupy separate container space and do not share packing volumes.
Weather and other environmental effects on flight are ignored.
Puerto Rico is treated as flat when geographic distances are converted to service circles.
Hospitals can store all medicine delivered before it is consumed.
Average sortie time and average payload are treated as stable enough that completion time can be replaced by inverse drone count.
The sum of individual maximum flight distances is treated as a proxy for reconnaissance capability.
Circular Euclidean service regions, an approximate coastline, and a one-way B transfer radius are treated as sufficient rough-location constraints.
A complete delivery flight including charging fits within a two-hour period, and hospital flights return while container-transfer flights do not.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Prompt-supplied dimensions, shipping volumes, payloads, speeds, flight times, and camera availability for drone types A-H feed fleet scoring, packing, range, and scheduling interfaces.
Cargo-bay and medicine-package dimensions, medicine weights, and cargo-container geometry define the nominal packing domain.
The paper converts the five hospitals' daily demand into 7 MED1, 2 MED2, and 4 MED3 packages per supply day.
The displayed three-by-three pairwise-comparison matrix produces weights 0.2051, 0.7167, and 0.0783 for time, medicine amount, and reconnaissance.
A minimum of 120 supply units and a score of 0.6 at that threshold anchor the medicine-amount normalization.
Nominal container, H-drone, and D-drone volumes define the volume-based maximum-drone normalizer used by the time proxy.
Maximum ranges and B-drone shipping volume define the paper's reference reconnaissance-range sum.
Five hospital coordinates, an approximate coastline, B/D delivery radii, and a B transfer radius define the rough siting overlays.
The external 3DBP service receives allocated drone, bay, and medicine cuboids and returns feasibility and packing configurations.
Road, highway, populated-place, service-range, hospital, coastline, and rough-area images are downsampled and converted to candidate-pixel layers.
The reported cargo-container coordinates A=(18.40,-66.12), B=(18.21,-65.82), and C=(18.43,-66.51) feed the flight timetable.
A ten-hour operating day, two-hour flight periods, one-hour charging, packed inventories, hospital identifiers, and thirty reconnaissance B drones parameterize the schedule.

models.summary: MU-B-2019-1908904-001: Convert judgments about delivery time, medicine amount, and reconnaissance into criterion weights and a consistency screen.
MU-B-2019-1908904-002: Convert medicine counts into supply days and then into a bounded score anchored at 120 days.
MU-B-2019-1908904-003: Approximate completion time by aggregate drone throughput, then replace it with normalized drone count.
MU-B-2019-1908904-004: Normalize the sum of maximum drone ranges against a volume-limited all-B reference fleet.
MU-B-2019-1908904-005: Select the next drone that maximizes the AHP-weighted normalized score until no candidate improves it.
MU-B-2019-1908904-006: Estimate ideal medicine days after subtracting drone and bay volume from container volume.
MU-B-2019-1908904-007: Compute B and D round-trip delivery radii plus the B inter-container transfer radius.
MU-B-2019-1908904-008: Choose three connected rough areas that jointly reach all hospitals with B and D service circles.
MU-B-2019-1908904-009: Scale the ideal plan, allocate goods by hospital responsibility, and maximize the retained fraction using a 3D packing API.
MU-B-2019-1908904-010: Score candidate points by standardized road and populated-place pixels within reconnaissance range.
MU-B-2019-1908904-011: Assign medicine deliveries, transfers, charging cycles, and road reconnaissance over two-hour periods.
MU-B-2019-1908904-012: Perturb the common loaded-distance factor and rerun range radii and container coordinates.
MU-B-2019-1908904-013: Change one criterion weight, split the offset equally over the other two, and rerun greedy fleet selection.
MU-B-2019-1908904-014: Preserve the implemented greedy score, hard-coded bisection quantities, and raster score as evidence about the body models.

results_trace.summary: AHP reports weights (0.2051, 0.7167, 0.0783), extracted lambda_max=3.0183, and CR=0.0158<0.1.
The ideal volume-stage greedy result is 121 B drones, 54 D drones, and 3 H drones.
Residual nominal volume yields an ideal 411-day medicine-duration claim before geometric packing waste.
The baseline range equations report B and D round-trip delivery radii of 23.4 km and 8 km, plus a 42.5 km B transfer range.
The rough-location overlay divides feasible service into Areas A, B, and C with A acting as the central transfer node.
Realistic packing reports A=(42 D,1 H), B=(39 B,1 H), C=(60 B,1 H), hence 99 B, 42 D, and 3 H overall.
Container utilizations are 77.60, 89.34, and 81.64 percent, averaging 82.86 percent.
After day one, every hospital is reported to hold at least twelve days of medicine.
The timetable claims all delivery ends after day five with 359 medicine-support days at every hospital.
Changing the loaded-distance factor to 0.825 or 0.775 changes the reported B/D radii and shifts coordinates by at most about 0.01 degree in Table 5.
AHP sensitivity reports maximum changes of 9.92 percent for B count, 33.3 percent for D count, and 2.4 percent for medicine days.
The conclusion reports five-day delivery, 359 supply days, road reconnaissance, and about nine populated places within reconnaissance range.

contributions.summary: Compresses a long operational pipeline into stage outputs and bounded case results in the summary before expanding it in the body.
Separates delivery time, medicine duration, and reconnaissance before applying explicit stakeholder weights.
Normalizes unlike operational criteria so every marginal fleet change has a visible decision score.
Uses a greedy marginal-update narrative that makes candidate evaluation, state update, and stopping intent inspectable.
Labels the residual-volume duration as an ideal upper bound and anticipates geometric packing waste.
Translates flight specifications into map-visible delivery and transfer geometry before choosing sites.
Assigns each rough site a distinct hospital and transfer role rather than selecting three disconnected points.
Connects site responsibility to container-specific B/D and medicine allocation before invoking a packing oracle.
Replaces rough visual placement with a declared two-feature pixel score over roads and populated places.
Converts aggregate fleet capacity into a repeated-flight timetable and reserves thirty B drones for reconnaissance.
Perturbs both a physical range premise and stakeholder weights after final decisions exist.
Returns locations, fleets, duration, reconnaissance limits, and utilization tradeoffs to HELP in direct operational prose.

writing_logic.summary: The summary opens with blocked post-hurricane access, names medicine delivery and road reconnaissance, then compresses AHP weighting, greedy fleet selection, rough siting, realistic packing, pixel siting, timetable construction, sensitivity, and final recommendations.
The introduction converts disaster context and heterogeneous drones into three measurable success criteria, making the later AHP stage predictable before technical detail begins.
Assumptions and notation bound range, charging, packing, weather, terrain, storage, communications, entities, units, and output symbols before those choices become hidden inside formulas.
The report fixes three containers from hospital reach and charging flexibility, then uses the flow diagram to route that deployment count into criterion weighting and packing.
AHP keeps time, medicine amount, and reconnaissance separate; three normalization subsections produce f(D), g(n), and h(x) before CE combines them.
CE drives a marginal greedy fleet whose ideal volume balance produces a 411-day upper bound, and the prose explicitly hands that optimistic state to a realistic packing stage.
B/D delivery-return radii and B transfer range become a map overlay; Areas A-C then assign hospital responsibility, D drones, and medicine types across containers.
The 70-percent initialization, allocation rules, external packing oracle, and bisection replace ideal counts with realized container inventories and utilization.
Rough areas, realized ranges, roads, and populated places become standardized raster features whose weighted maxima yield the three exact coordinates.

Exact coordinates and packed inventories become a five-slot-per-day timetable; the sensitivity section then revisits range and AHP interfaces before conclusion and the HELP letter reassemble the decision.

visual-quantity-comparator interpretation: Lead from a named table, figure, or timetable to a scoped quantitative claim. Occurrences=21; order=visual pointer -> quantity -> comparator -> case value -> bounded interpretation; slots=[visual]; [metric]; [baseline]; [value]; [meaning]; variants=shown in; as we can see; we find; the result; therefore; boundary=A plotted configuration, local sensitivity result, or API packing image is not external validation.

criterion weight to operational choice: Connect stated priorities to weights, a scalar score, and the selected fleet or location. Occurrences=6; order=priority rationale -> weight -> normalized criterion -> combined score -> decision; slots=[stake]; [weight]; [criterion]; [score]; [choice]; variants=most important; smallest proportion; weight; comprehensive; choose; boundary=AHP weights express judgments; they do not establish calibration, fairness, or global robustness.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: The summary's complete need-to-stage-to-result chain is highly scannable, but award status does not prove that this structure caused the outcome.
The early flow diagram plausibly reduces cognitive load across a coupled packing-siting-scheduling task; this is a clarity hypothesis rather than evidence of correctness.
The service-circle diagram makes the functional role of each rough area immediately visible despite missing projection and source-data detail.
Placing realized inventories, utilization, map layers, and exact coordinates next to one another plausibly strengthens decision traceability while retaining documented conflicts.
The HELP letter repeats the technical chain in operational language and states a reconnaissance/utilization tradeoff, closing the stakeholder loop conditionally.

weaknesses.summary: The extracted text reports lambda_max=3.0183, while focused visual inspection can plausibly be read as 3.0153. The ambiguity must be resolved from the source matrix rather than silently normalized.

The delivery-time expression mixes route distance/speed with T0 declared in minutes, while the prose later replaces heterogeneous route, speed, payload, and charging terms by inverse drone count without a dimensional reconciliation.

The displayed Dmax numerator uses 3Vc-3(Vh-120Vm), whose parentheses and sign can add rather than reserve medicine volume. The expression, units, and intended three-container accounting require reconstruction.

The ideal result is B121/D54/H3, the appendix initializes a different D constant, the real packing contains B99/D42/H3, and the conclusion states B121/D42 while omitting H; these are distinct states and cannot be merged.

The displayed 411-day numerator appears to use one Vc while the surrounding calculation concerns three containers, and its denominator notation does not clearly separate daily package counts from package volumes.

The prose presents a bisection over a retained percentage beginning at 70 percent, but the appendix first hard-codes a 339-day fleet scale. The searched quantity and reported 359-day endpoint are therefore not reproduced by the printed code.
The body assigns road/highway weight 0.6 and populated-place weight 0.4, but appendix A.4 implements 0.4 and 0.6 respectively, so the reported coordinates lack a unique scoring specification.
The raster-scoring function modifies road and city arrays in place while evaluating candidates. Later scores can therefore depend on candidate and function-call order rather than only on location.
The five-day 359-day claim is not accompanied by a complete inventory, payload, route, charge-port, battery, turnaround, and terminal-state conservation ledger for every timetable cell.
A maximum 33.3-percent change in D-drone count is characterized as small and stable. A local one-factor plot does not establish end-to-end robustness or justify that interpretation.
The appendix uses hard-coded normalizers 394 and 256*52.67. Their derivation and consistency with the displayed Nmax and Dmax formulas are not demonstrated.
The appendix fixes 339 in the B/D scaling formulas even though the body reports 411 ideal days and 359 realized days, leaving the bisection target and final fleet unreconciled.
The authors acknowledge that using one maximum-distance reduction rate for every drone type suppresses power, weight, speed, and endurance differences.
The authors acknowledge that treating the island as flat introduces distance error where altitude varies.
The prose says the rough-location map is the following Figure 5, while the displayed caption is Figure 2.
Table 3 contains realized container inventories and space use but repeats the title Pairwise comparison matrix of hierarchy.
The conclusion prints container B longitude -65.28, whereas Table 4, body text, sensitivity table, plotting code, and the operative configuration use approximately -65.82.
The bibliography has only three entries, while most vehicle specifications, hospital demand, coordinates, road/city rasters, map imagery, and operational parameters lack reproducible source bindings.

independent_extensions.summary: Recompute the displayed AHP matrix, resolve the eigenvalue glyph, elicit judgments from multiple stakeholders, and report disagreement and weight intervals.
Replace inverse drone count with a unit-consistent event model covering route, payload, charging, queueing, loading, unloading, and hospital service time.
Replace summed maximum range with unique road/population coverage under sensor footprint, overlap, route continuity, energy reserve, and return feasibility.
Benchmark the greedy fleet against MILP, CP-SAT, dynamic programming, or bounded enumeration and publish iteration traces and optimality gaps.
Use a projected coordinate system, terrain-aware energy model, vehicle-specific loaded range, coastline geometry, and robust service constraints for rough siting.
Freeze the exact packing instance and API response, define orientations and weight limits, reproduce it locally, and compare the heuristic allocation with exact packing bounds.
Publish immutable road/city rasters, CRS, thresholds, candidate masks, and coordinate transforms; run body and code weights separately and test order invariance.
Encode every timetable cell in a conservation-tested time-indexed model with batteries, charge ports, turnaround, maintenance, transfers, routes, and safe terminal states.
Run global and joint uncertainty over demand, range, payload, weather, terrain, AHP weights, packing feasibility, raster data, schedules, and decision switches.
Generate tables, maps, conclusion coordinates, and the HELP letter from one frozen result object so B longitude and fleet counts cannot diverge.
Build a claim-level provenance ledger for every drone, medicine, hospital, map, road, city, container, charging, and API datum.
Repair and package all appendix code with redacted credentials, pinned dependencies, fixtures, deterministic tests, body-code parity checks, and one-command reproduction.
